text:
maria-support: seeing a spike of 502/504s for hostedapi in eu-1 starting ~11:02. customer reports long-tail timeouts on streaming completions. lots of correlation ids show upstream auth backend 504s. sample: X-Request-ID=rcpt-9f2a

kevin-sre: thanks — any recent deploys or config changes? p95 latency for auth?

maria-support: no infra deploys in the last hour, but auth team rotated a couple of tokens at 10:58. p95 auth latency jumped from 40ms -> 700ms around 11:00. 502s trace: envoy -> midproxy -> billing-auth (504).

raj-eng: could be a tenant-specific cache stampede when TTLs hit. if many tenants revalidate at same time, auth backend gets thrashed -> midproxy returns 504 and edge surfaces 502. do we have metrics for auth cache misses?

olivia-platform: adding some logs and a short curl repro. curious if this reproduces locally:
```bash
for i in {1..40}; do \\\curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Tenant: acme" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/completions" -d '{"input":"hello","max_tokens":1024}' &
 done; wait
```

maria-support: attached a snippet from edge logs (filtered):
```
[11:02:13] envoy: cluster_upstream_rq 502 upstream_host=midproxy-2 id=rcpt-9f2a
[11:02:13] midproxy: upstream call billing-auth POST /validate -> 504 (timeout)
[11:02:13] hostproxy: stream terminated: connection: h2  id=rcpt-9f2a
```

kevin-sre: this matches cache-regeneration stampede. also seeing h2 WINDOW_UPDATE errors on some upstreams (h2 window exhaustion). two suggested triage actions: 1) temporarily increase auth cache TTL / enable jittered backoff on revalidation, 2) add a short-rate limit on edge per-tenant to avoid bursty revalidations. can we patch TTL from control plane?

maria-support: I can toggle the TTL for tenant `acme` from 60s -> 300s via control plane, want me to?

raj-eng: do that but also capture traces for a few request ids to confirm resolution path. run: `curl -v -H "X-Request-ID: test-rcpt" ...` and paste the trace id here.

deploy-bot: deploy:auth-service v2.14.0 rolled back (was released 2026-02-10T10:55Z) by @kevin-sre — reason: token rotation heuristics caused bursty revalidations.

maria-support: rolled acme TTL to 300s at 11:10. after ~3min the 502/504 counts dropped by ~85% in eu-1. attaching quick dashboard snap: auth_cache_miss_rate down, envoy_upstream_5xx down.

kevin-sre: good. follow-ups: 1) audit token rotation window to add jitter and stagger across tenants, 2) implement adaptive per-tenant soft-throttling at edge to protect backend, 3) add an alert for sudden auth cache miss spikes. i've opened ENG-3456 for the work.

olivia-platform: noted. can we also add a short lived fallback rule to route tenant traffic to dedicated auth replicas when miss-rate > 20%? that could avoid edge 502 surface.

maria-support: customer updated, they saw failure rate drop. marking as customer-resolved for now. will keep thread open until ENG-3456 has owner updates. :white_check_mark:

gw-bot: incident:edge-502-spike-eu1 -> mitigated (TTL tweak) at 11:13, incident id inc-20260210-2089

kevin-sre: final notes for postmortem: correlate auth rotation job windows, adjust default cache TTL to tolerate rotation storms, and add a quick runbook step: "if 502/504 spike in region with matching auth-cache-miss jump -> increase cache TTL and enable tenant throttling".

maria-support: thanks team. closing for now unless customer reopens.
